title: Job 16
paragraphs: ¹ Then Job answered and said: ² "I have heard all of this before. You are miserable comforters, every one of you. ³ Will your windy words never end? What is driving you to keep answering? ⁴ I could speak just as you do — if you were in my place, I could heap words together against you and shake my head at you. ⁵ I could strengthen you with my mouth and move my lips to ease your pain.

⁶ But when I speak, my pain is not relieved; and when I hold back, it does not leave me. ⁷ Surely he has worn me out now; he has made my whole community desolate. ⁸ He has shriveled me up — and this is evidence against me; my wasting body rises up and testifies to my face. ⁹ He tears me apart in his anger and hates me; he gnashes his teeth at me; my enemy pierces me with his eyes. ¹⁰ People gape at me with open mouths; they strike my cheek with contempt; they mass together against me.

¹¹ God has handed me over to the ungodly and thrown me into the hands of the wicked. ¹² I was living in peace, but he shattered me; he seized me by the neck and smashed me to pieces, then set me up as his target. ¹³ His archers surround me; he pierces my kidneys without mercy and pours out my bile on the ground. ¹⁴ He breaks through me, breach after breach; he charges at me like a warrior. ¹⁵ I have sewn sackcloth over my skin and buried my brow in the dust.

¹⁶ My face is red from weeping, and dark shadows ring my eyes — ¹⁷ though there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is sincere. ¹⁸ O earth, do not cover my blood; let my cry find no resting place. ¹⁹ Even now, my witness is in heaven; my advocate is on high. ²⁰ My friends scorn me, but my eyes pour out tears to God.
²¹ Oh, that someone would plead with God on behalf of a person, as one pleads for a friend! ²² For only a few years will pass before I go down the path from which I will not return.
